taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. On September 30, 2026, North America is in Daylight Saving Time, so Eastern Time (ET) is Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4).
2. Spain is also in Daylight Saving Time, so Madrid is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).
3. Madrid (UTC+2) is 6 hours ahead of Eastern Daylight Time (UTC-4).
4. Adding 6 hours to 5:00 PM (17:00) EDT on September 30, 2026 gives 11:00 PM (23:00) on September 30, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time zone (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru does not observe Daylight Saving Time). 

To convert 12:00 UTC to your local time, subtract 5 hours from 12:00 UTC:
12:00 UTC - 5 hours = 07:00 PET on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Central European Summer Time (CEST) is UTC+2. Tokyo, which uses Japan Standard Time (JST), is UTC+9. This makes Tokyo 7 hours ahead of CEST.

Adding 7 hours to 9:00 AM on June 1, 2026, brings the time to 4:00 PM (16:00) on the same day in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Time Zones on October 11, 2026:**
   * **PDT (Pacific Daylight Time):** UTC-7 (Daylight Saving Time is active in the US until November 1).
   * **CEST (Central European Summer Time, Madrid):** UTC+2 (Daylight Saving Time is active in Spain until October 25).

2. **Time Difference:**
   * Madrid (CEST) is 9 hours ahead of PDT (UTC+2 vs. UTC-7).

3. **Calculation:**
   * 11:59 PM PDT on October 11, 2026 + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Pacific Standard Time (PST) is UTC-8. On March 3, 2026, standard time is in effect in both the US Pacific time zone and in Madrid, Spain (Central European Time, UTC+1). 

Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PST. Adding 9 hours to March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST brings us to March 4, 2026 at 8:59 AM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert 10:00 AM CET (Central European Time) on February 2, 2026, to your local time in Los Angeles, California:

1. On February 2, 2026, both regions are on standard time: CET is UTC+1, and Los Angeles (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8.
2. Los Angeles is 9 hours behind CET.
3. Subtracting 9 hours from 10:00 AM CET on February 2, 2026, gives 1:00 AM PST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9, while Lima, Peru observes Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5. Neither region observes Daylight Saving Time in 2026. 

This means Lima is 14 hours behind Japan Standard Time. Subtracting 14 hours from May 5, 2026, at 08:00 JST gives May 4, 2026, at 18:00 PET.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 28, 2026:
- **Pacific Time (PT)** is in Daylight Saving Time (PDT), which is **UTC-7** (North American DST ends on November 1, 2026).
- **Madrid, Spain** is in standard Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1** (European DST ends on October 25, 2026).

The time difference between PDT (UTC-7) and CET (UTC+1) is +8 hours. 

Adding 8 hours to October 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) PDT results in October 29, 2026, at 07:59 AM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the corresponding time in Madrid, Spain, we need to consider Daylight Saving Time rules for both locations on October 30, 2026:

1. **Eastern Time (ET):** In the United States, Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026). Thus, on October 30, 2026, Eastern Time is in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is **UTC-4**.
2. **Madrid, Spain:** In Europe, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Thus, on October 30, 2026, Madrid has already switched back to Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1**.

The time difference between EDT (UTC-4) and CET (UTC+1) is 5 hours (Madrid is 5 hours ahead).

* 9:00 AM EDT + 5 hours = 2:00 PM (14:00) CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in New York:

1. **Central European Time (CET)**: In Europe, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Thus, on October 27, 2026, Central Europe is observing standard time (CET, which is UTC+1).
2. **Eastern Daylight Time (EDT)**: In the US, Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026). Thus, on October 27, 2026, New York is still observing Daylight Saving Time (EDT, which is UTC-4).
3. **Difference**: EDT (UTC-4) is 5 hours behind CET (UTC+1).
4. **Calculation**: Subtracting 5 hours from 18:00 CET gives 13:00 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the contest deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain, we need to consider the timezone offsets on November 2, 2026:

1. **Pacific Time (PT):** The US transitions from Daylight Saving Time to Standard Time on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026). Therefore, on November 2, PT is in Pacific Standard Time (**PST**, which is **UTC-8**).
2. **Madrid Time:** Europe transitions from Daylight Saving Time to Standard Time on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, on November 2, Madrid is in Central European Time (**CET**, which is **UTC+1**).

Madrid is **9 hours ahead** of Pacific Time on this date (UTC+1 vs UTC-8).

Adding 9 hours to November 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT:
- 11:59 PM PT + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on the next day (November 3, 2026).

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the contest deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Pacific Time (PT)**: On March 20, 2026, the US is observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7), as US Daylight Saving Time begins on March 8, 2026.
2. **Madrid Time**: Spain observes Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) on March 20, 2026, as European Daylight Saving Time does not start until March 29, 2026.
3. **Difference**: Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time (UTC+1 vs. UTC-7).

Adding 8 hours to March 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) PDT brings us to March 21, 2026, at 7:59 AM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the time from Central European Time (CET) to your local time in Los Angeles, Pacific Daylight Time (PDT):

1. On March 25, 2026, Los Angeles will be observing Daylight Saving Time (PDT, which is UTC-7).
2. On March 25, 2026, Central Europe has not yet switched to daylight saving time, so it will be on Standard Time (CET, which is UTC+1).
3. The time difference between CET (UTC+1) and PDT (UTC-7) is 8 hours.
4. Subtracting 8 hours from 12:00 PM (12:00) CET gives 4:00 AM (04:00) PDT on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Eastern Time (ET) on October 12, 2026**: The US will be in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.
2. **Madrid Local Time on October 12, 2026**: Spain will be in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.
3. **Time Difference**: Madrid is 6 hours ahead of Eastern Time.
4. **Conversion**: 12:00 AM (midnight, the very start of October 12) EDT plus 6 hours is 6:00 AM (06:00) on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in Madrid local time:

1. **Understand AoE (Anywhere on Earth):** AoE corresponds to UTC-12. Therefore, 23:59 AoE on October 9, 2026, is equivalent to October 10, 2026, at 11:59 UTC.
2. **Determine Madrid's time zone:** On October 10, 2026, Madrid will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2 (since Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on October 25, 2026).
3. **Convert to local time:** Adding 2 hours to 11:59 UTC on October 10, 2026, gives 13:59 CEST on October 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On August 14, 2026, both regions observe daylight saving time:
- Pacific Time (PT) is in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7.
- Madrid, Spain is in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

This puts Madrid 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time. Adding 9 hours to 12:00 PM (noon) PT on August 14, 2026 gives 9:00 PM (21:00) on the same day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Identify the time zones:**
   * **IST (Indian Standard Time):** UTC+5:30
   * **Madrid Local Time:** On November 10, 2026, Daylight Saving Time will have ended (ended October 25, 2026), putting Madrid in Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1**.

2. **Calculate the time difference:**
   * Madrid (UTC+1) is **4 hours and 30 minutes behind** IST (UTC+5:30).

3. **Convert the time:**
   * 11:59 PM IST (23:59 IST) minus 4 hours and 30 minutes equals **19:29** (7:29 PM) on the same date, November 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Lima, Peru:

1. **Nepal Time (NPT)** is UTC+5:45. The deadline is 5:00 PM (17:00) on April 2, 2026.
2. Converting 17:00 NPT to UTC gives **11:15 UTC** on April 2, 2026.
3. **Lima, Peru Time (PET)** is UTC-5 year-round. Subtracting 5 hours from 11:15 UTC gives **06:15** local time on April 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain, we first look at the time zones active on October 6, 2026:

1. **Adelaide, Australia:** Daylight saving time begins on the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026). Therefore, on October 6, Adelaide will be on Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT), which is **UTC+10:30**.
2. **Madrid, Spain:** Central European Summer Time (CEST) remains in effect until the last Sunday of October. Therefore, on October 6, Madrid will be on CEST, which is **UTC+2**.

The time difference between Adelaide (UTC+10:30) and Madrid (UTC+2) is **8 hours and 30 minutes** (Adelaide is ahead).

Subtracting 8 hours and 30 minutes from 10:00 AM on October 6, 2026, gives 1:30 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the local deadline in Madrid, Spain (CEST, UTC+2):

1. **Sydney Timezone on October 3, 2026:** Daylight Saving Time in Sydney starts on the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026). Therefore, on Saturday, October 3, 2026, Sydney is on Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST, UTC+10).
2. **Madrid Timezone on October 3, 2026:** Spain is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).
3. **Time Difference:** Madrid is 8 hours behind Sydney (UTC+10 minus UTC+2).
4. **Conversion:** Subtracting 8 hours from 6:00 PM (18:00) Sydney time on October 3, 2026, gives 10:00 AM (10:00) on the same day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
